sentences.text: Revenue grew from $404.5 million in FY2016 to $5.93 billion in FY2025, a 34.8% compound rate [F1][F10][F196].
Growth ran between 43.1% and 64.2% a year from FY2018 to FY2021 [D80][D218], then slowed to 0.1% in FY2023 [D311].
The FY2017 jump, 104.0% growth to $825 million [D36][F2], came from more ads delivered and the self-serve platform launched in November 2016 [P81].
The cited filings do not explain the FY2023 stall, so it should not be read as a cyclical trend [D311].
Advertising Revenue was $5.19 billion in FY2025, 87.4% of revenue, and grew 5.8% [S39][D536][D537].
Advertising added 5.3pp and Other Revenue 5.4pp of the 10.6% growth [D538][D545][D406].
Other Revenue reached $745 million, 12.6% of revenue, after growing 62.9% [S42][D543][D544].
The filing credits advertising growth to about 17% more impressions, partly offset by about 10% lower price per impression, and Other Revenue to more subscribers [P24].
Operating costs grew 5.1% against revenue growth of 10.6%, and incremental operating margin was 44.8% [D423][D406][D429].
Net loss shrank 34.0% [D408] while loss per diluted share shrank 35.7% [D410], as diluted shares rose 2.1% to 1,694.6 million [D425][X150].
Operating margin of -9.0% in FY2025 [F30] is the window high [D554], against a -32.4% median [D555].
It improved 5.7pp, with cost of revenue adding 1.1pp, R&D 1.3pp and other lines 3.3pp [D419][D431][D432][D433].
The filing says sales and marketing fell $42.4 million on prior-year event timing and $19.9 million of restructuring [P22].
The largest move, 315.1pp in FY2018 [D92], came as stock-based compensation fell from $2.64 billion to $538 million [X82][X83], which the filing ties to lower G&A stock awards [P75][P76].
Net margin of -7.8% [F50] sits 1.2pp above operating margin of -9.0% [F30], helped by $68.9 million of other income [X130][P18].
Operating cash flow was $656 million in FY2025 [F80], 11.1% of revenue [D394], against a net loss of $460.5 million [F40].
Free cash flow of $437 million [F100] was a 7.4% margin [D393], equal to the window high [D560], after $219 million of capex [F90].
The filing attributes the gap mainly to $1.0 billion of stock-based compensation and $163.6 million of D&A, with $96.7 million of debt-extinguishment gains among the adjustments [P13].
Cash generation is real but leans on non-cash pay, equal to 155.0% of operating cash flow [D396].
Net cash became net debt of $596 million in FY2025 [D399], -10.1% of revenue [D400], down from $1.44 billion in FY2021 [D211].
On net cash to revenue the company ranks at the 0th percentile of five internet peers, against a 45.0% median [D578][D579].
The 2033 Notes raised $1.47 billion net and funded the repurchase of $1.4 billion of 2026 to 2028 notes [P2][P1].
Buybacks of $751 million [X156] equalled 171.7% of free cash flow [D402], and diluted shares still rose 2.1% [D425].
The balance sheet has moved from cash to debt while returns outrun free cash flow [D399][D402], leaving less room for error.
Net losses persist: every year from FY2016 to FY2025 is loss-making, including $460.5 million in FY2025 [R1][F40].
Stock-based compensation was 17.1% of revenue [R2][D390], $1.02 billion [X90], and 191.1% of the operating loss [D404].
Stock pay is the main reason cash flow looks better than the loss.
Buybacks exceeded free cash flow in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 [R4][D307][D354][D402], and net cash has fallen four years running [R3][D399].
Operating margin holding above -9.0% [F30][D554] in the FY2026 10-K confirms the trend; a return to -14.7% [F29] reverses it.
Net cash below -$596 million [D399] in the FY2026 10-K confirms the shift to debt, and a move back above -$268 million [D351] reverses it.
Buybacks above 171.7% of free cash flow [D402] would confirm returns outrunning cash, and a return below 142.3% [D354] reverses it, in the FY2026 10-K.
